items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: It turns out it was Lester Young. They were — God bless them. When I heard that music, when I first heard it it was like there was something about it that touched me according to how I felt about things.

ctx.x: Well it was a compliment. So. So over my shoulders I have pictures of a few of my musical heroes including Cannonball Adderley, Lester Young, Count Basie. And I know you worked with Dinah Washington. So the music of these people may be looked at as less spiritual than the music you played with Pharoah Sanders. So I’m wondering how you think of that music in society. What is the role of that music in society?

I don’t think it’s any less spiritual. I think it’s just a different approach. Remember I mentioned earlier that it’s about adding something, taking something away, how you manage those conditions as they flow into — and conceptually these individuals are doing their thing accordingly, more or less effort, more or less intent to express, maybe not a spiritual situation but a statement that references the moment of who they are individually and collectively. As I profess, if you will initially, earlier, it can’t…
That’s an amazing story. I’ve had similar experiences but it was on recordings and you’re so touched by something that you’re compelled to go find out more about that.
